format: One row per page x width (audit/pages.js, widths [1280, 3440]). THERE IS NO `score` OR `grade` FIELD ANY MORE, and their absence is the point: measured against eighteen hand-rated screenshots the old aggregate came out ANTI-correlated with how pages look (Pearson -0.393; against DOM node count Spearman -0.519), because it counted findings and findings scale with content, so it rewarded emptiness -- it handed grade A / 96 to the worst-looking page in the corpus and its single lowest score to the best, and it never emitted below 70 across a 36-point reality. Every RULE survived unchanged; only the average was removed. Evidence: ai/2026-08-17/vision-baseline/; the removal and the new ranking: ai/2026-08-17/tier-calibration/. Rank by `counts` -- score.js's `worst_first` is the one comparator (high desc, then med, then low), and it makes no quality claim: this tier is a DEFECT WORKLIST and taste.json is the tier that ranks quality. Every row carries what it takes to rank -- counts, metrics -- plus a compact, UNCAPPED per-instance issue summary (`rules`: {rule, title, sev}, one entry per finding; no selector, DOM path, proposed fix or human `detail` text). `rules.length` always equals `counts.total` for every row, by construction, so a row can never silently lose its worst finding the way an old undocumented 3-4-entry cap sometimes did. Full finding detail is deliberately never stored: audit/page.js's open() re-measures a row live via frame() the instant it is opened. Regenerate: a headless Playwright pass driving analyze() and rate() from ONE probe model per row, over every url in pages.js at every width -- fresh browser context every 40 navigations, the module imported in its own page.evaluate(), goto waitUntil:'load' and never networkidle. taste.json is written by the same pass, so the two files always describe the same measurement.
